Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pladdrr 5.1.0

5.1.0 collects the 2026-11 audit round: safety and robustness fixes (sessions that died, memory read or requested out of bounds, errors that named neither the file nor the cause), plus corrections that change numbers a user can see or make a call that used to succeed raise. Each of the latter moves toward what the Praat application returns, and each states by how much. The safety and robustness items are listed after “Behaviour changes”.

Numbers that change

  • Options passed to Praat script commands now select the option Praat would select. pladdrr’s library-mode form layer (src/uiform_libmode.cpp, the script-only stand-in for Praat’s Ui.cpp) stored Praat’s base argument — the number an option list starts at — in the field’s subtract slot instead of converting it (Ui.cpp:1201 thy subtract = ( base == 1 ? 0 : 1 );), so every CHOICE/OPTIONMENU argument reached the command one option too low (Ltas: Get mean: 0, 0, "energy" returned the dB mean and "dB" the sones mean; Pitch: Get standard deviation: 0, 0, "hertz" the ERB figure), every 0-based CHOICEx list one option too high (Pitch: Get value at time: …, "nearest" interpolated like "linear"), and the first option of a CHOICE_ENUM — Pitch’s own default unit "hertz", "none", "nearest" — raised Field 'Unit' must not have the value 'hertz'. where Praat answers a number. This is the script layer only: it applies to PraatInterpreter$run() and praat_run_script() alike, not to the R6 or direct wrappers, which pass their own integers and were already checked against Praat. It is not only a string-layer bug: a numeric third argument changed meaning, so Get mean: 0, 0, 1 (energy in Praat’s own enum) returned -8.19 dB before and 42.85 dB now, and a script that compensated by shifting its own option strings, or by adding one to a number, must undo that. Among the families now answered instead of refused: the twelve Formant: Get ... commands whose Unit argument is Praat’s kFormant_unit choice (all twelve used to error on their default; the enum offers "hertz" and "bark", and "erb" is refused by Praat 6.4.27 too), and Intensity: Get mean, whose default "energy" came out 4.06 dB low (84.0703382556 where Praat prints 88.1298604765).

  • Reading FLAC, MP3, OGG and other av-decoded files no longer changes the level or folds the channels. The fallback reader divided the decoded samples by their own peak instead of the format’s full scale, so the same tone came back 6.02 dB hotter from a lossless FLAC than from the WAV it was converted from, and it ignored the channel count, so a 2 x N stereo file arrived as a 1 x 2N mono Sound of twice the length. It now scales by full scale (2^31, the S32LE that av::read_audio_bin() hands back) and de-interleaves into one row per channel. The substitution itself is announced with a catchable pladdrr_decoder_fallback warning instead of a console message, so a script that insists on the native reader can turn it into an error. Known limit, documented in ?Sound: AAC/MP4 encoder delay is not trimmed (Praat has no reader for those containers, so there is no oracle behaviour to reproduce).

  • Intensity$get_mean()’s averaging_method sent Praat’s averaging codes one too low, so the documented default "energy" returned the median, "sones" returned the energy average and "db" the sones average. The table now matches Praat’s Intensity_averaging enum ("median" 0, "energy" 1, "sones" 2, "db" 3) and an unknown string errors instead of quietly averaging in medians. How far a number moves is the gap between the median and the energy mean of the contour, so it depends on the material and is not bounded: on the level-stepped signal the tests use it is 0.39 dB (87.74 -> 88.13 dB), on a stationary file it is 8e-06 dB, and on a file that is mostly below its own analysis threshold the old median sat on the floor and the answer was the -300 dB floor value where the energy average is 54.93 dB. check_audio_quality()’s mean_intensity_db is that same call and moves with it. Intensity$get_statistics()’s "mean" metric and print()’s “Mean intensity” line now use the same energy average, so all three agree. The integer APIs keep their numbers (intensity_get_mean_direct(x, 0, 0, 0L) is the median before and after — it used to add one, which is why the string layer was off by one, not the integer layer); their documentation is what was corrected, and it now names 0 median, 1 energy, 2 sones, 3 dB, which is also Praat’s Intensity_averaging order. Passing a raw integer to Intensity$get_mean() (e.g. averaging_method = 0L, which silently meant “median”) is no longer accepted; it errors and names the four strings. "db" is Praat’s legacy two-argument Intensity: Get mean.

  • BREAKING CHANGE (numbers move). Ltas$get_mean(), $get_means_batch() and $get_standard_deviation() with unit = "energy" or unit = "sones" returned the linear average — the mean of 10^(dB/10) or of 2^(dB/10) — where Praat’s Ltas: Get mean averages in that domain and then converts the result back, so they now report the dB number Praat prints. Before: on a one-second speech LTAS ltas$get_mean(0, 0, unit = "energy") returned 14170.064098 (unit = "sones" returned the deceptively dB-shaped 0.900002); after, the same call returns 41.513718 dB, which is what Praat prints and what 10*log10() of the old answer already gave. Nothing marks the change at runtime: a column stored by 5.0.5 under unit = "energy" was simply wrong by three decades, and re-running the old script now silently gives different numbers, so recompute anything you saved. ltas$get_standard_deviation(0, 0, unit = "energy") moved the same way (209963.529484 → 53.221439 dB).

  • Ltas$get_slope() and $get_local_peak_height() mapped unit = "dB" — their default — to Praat’s code 0, while Ltas_getSlope and Ltas_getLocalPeakHeight test for 3 (fon/Ltas.cpp:87, :95), so they returned a dimensionless ratio instead of a dB difference and could flip sign: get_slope(0, 1000, 1000, 4000) gave -0.115522, it now gives -31.906946 dB (Praat’s answer); get_slope(1000, 4000, 4000, 8000) changes sign, from +5.840895 to -15.995483. "energy" and "sones" results are unchanged, which is why v4.0.4’s table called them the working spellings — they were right by accident, because only the dB branch was broken.

  • Ltas band averages no longer interpolate between bins, matching Praat’s Ltas queries, which pass interpolate = false. The default unit = "dB" results move too, so “dB is unchanged” above would have been wrong: any band whose edges do not fall on bin edges changes, and how far depends on how far off they are. On inst/extdata/test.wav, get_mean(500, 2000) went from 10.717937 to 10.444981 dB; scanning 50 Hz-wide bands over 0-5500 Hz on an Ltas with a 100 Hz analysis bandwidth the movement reaches 8.41 dB, so a low band inside a single bin is the worst case, not an exception. Full-band means (fmin = fmax = 0, the usual call) are bit-identical to before, and every averaging method, unit string and band tested is now bit-identical to Praat 6.4.27 (tests/testthat/test-ltas-averaging-unit.R). An unknown unit string in an averaging query is now a pladdrr_input_error instead of a silent "energy", so this also BREAKS a script that had been passing a typo.

Behaviour changes

  • Ltas$get_value_at_frequency(), $get_minimum() and $get_maximum() took a unit argument and ignored it, so unit = "energy" or "sones" silently returned dB. They answer in the bins’ own dB (Praat’s dialogs for them have no unit), so they now accept only "dB" (any case) and raise a pladdrr_input_error for anything else. Behaviour change to expect: a call that passed another unit used to return the dB number and now raises.

Bug fixes

  • batch_process() rows for files that failed now carry error_class next to error (the first class of the condition, e.g. pladdrr_input_error). A worker turns a condition into a row so one bad file cannot lose the run, which means a tryCatch(pladdrr_data_loss = ) around the call can never see it; filter on error_class instead. The documentation says so.

  • The default worker count is the usable CPUs minus one only when there are more than two. With a 2-CPU allowance it was one worker, so batch_process(parallel = TRUE) silently ran serially.

  • An av-decoded file whose container reports no channel count (NA) is read as mono instead of failing with “invalid ‘dim’”.

  • Sizes that become allocations are validated up front. sound_create_tone(), sound_create_pure_tone() and sound_create_tone_complex() refuse a non-positive, non-finite or absurd duration / sampling_rate (a negative duration used to return a Sound with nx = -16000; 1e9 s asked for 4.4e13 samples), Matrix() / matrix_create_simple() refuse non-positive or oversized dimensions (a negative count built a corrupt object), and Excitation$to_formant() needs max_formants >= 1. All raise a classed pladdrr_input_error naming the argument. The limit is 2^29 cells (4 GiB of doubles), the same as the cochleagram bound.

  • The automatic thread count is capped at two when _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_ is set to anything but false, the way R CMD check --as-cran sets it and the way parallel already honours it. Before, only the R-level worker default followed it, so the C++ pool still used every core and CRAN’s timing check (CPU time over 2.5x elapsed) flagged the CPPS examples: a 3 s to_powercepstrogram_fast() + get_cpps_fast() ran at a CPU/elapsed ratio of 7.7 and now 2.0 under the variable. Outside R CMD check nothing changes, and an explicit pladdrr_threads(n) still wins.

  • Every class constructor that takes .xptr now refuses a pointer to a Praat object of another class with a pladdrr_input_error (“Not a Sound (found TextGrid)”), the check Matrix and PitchTier already had. Before, 10 constructors (Sound, Pitch, Formant, FormantTier, Intensity, IntensityTier, Excitation, MFCC, LFCC, TextGrid) re-interpreted the foreign object and the first query killed the R session (SIGSEGV, exit 139), and 21 more answered with another class’s numbers. Subclasses still pass (a Sound is a valid Matrix), and PowerCepstrogram does the same.

  • Sound$to_cochleagram(), $to_cochleagram_edb() and Spectrum$to_excitation() refuse a step size that cannot describe the result instead of asking Praat for it. df = 1e-9 is a 2.5 TB request: Linux answered with an allocation error, but macOS committed the pages and the kernel killed the whole R session (exit 137, invisible to tryCatch()). The size is now bounded in C++ (2^29 cochleagram cells, i.e. about 5.8 h of audio at the default steps; 10 000 excitation bands), so every door (R6, module, script) raises “… is not allowed”. dt, df, window_length, dtime and dfreq also raise a classed pladdrr_input_error naming the argument, and to_cochleagram_edb(dfreq = -1) no longer returns a Cochleagram with a negative band count. Behaviour change to expect: requests above those bounds used to run on Linux machines with enough memory and now raise.

  • Sound$to_cochleagram() on a very low-rate Sound no longer kills the R process. A sampling rate below ~67 Hz (with the default 0.03 s window) made the internal analysis window negative, and the FFT zero-padding step three functions away wrote outside a one-cell allocation: free(): invalid pointer, exit code 134, invisible to tryCatch() — the whole session died, along with anything an agent had in flight. It now raises, in every door (Sound$to_cochleagram(), the cochleagram_module door, and a script To Cochleagram:), with Praat’s own message for the case, “Analysis window too short.” — the guard Sound_to_Pitch has always had. Behaviour change to expect: at the default 0.03 s window the guard refuses any sampling rate below 200 Hz (the window needs 6 samples). Measured on the previous build those rates had no usable output — 67-133 Hz returned an all-NaN cochleagram (0 of 4352 cells finite), 150-199 Hz about 55% finite, the same degenerate shape as the still-accepted 200-500 Hz — but a script calling one of them now gets an error where it got a matrix of gaps.

  • A failed cochleagram or excitation conversion no longer contaminates every later Praat error in the session. Six catch blocks — five in src/cochleagram_wrappers.cpp and src/excitation_wrappers.cpp, plus the exported sound_extract_parts_pooled() — were the only ones that let a Praat error cross back into R without calling Melder_clearError(). Praat’s global error buffer only accumulates, and that call alone empties it, so after one bad conversion (Sound$to_cochleagram(df = 1e-9), Spectrum$to_excitation(erb_density = 1e-9)) every later error in the same R session was prefixed with the stale “not enough room for … elements” / “not converted to Cochleagram” text: an agent parsing an error got a message mixing two unrelated calls, and since Praat drops text that would overflow its 2000-character buffer, a saturated buffer loses later error text outright. (Eight further blocks do not clear either; they re-throw into an outer clearing catch instead of reaching R, so they are left alone.) The reason Praat actually gave now travels in the error it belongs to: those errors end with Praat’s own text (Praat error in Spectrum_to_Excitation: Out of memory: ...) via the package’s get_melder_error() helper, which previously had no callers at all. Matching the existing prefix keeps working; anything anchored to the end of the message must be updated.

  • as.matrix() no longer returns junk for the 39 of 41 object classes that had no method of their own. Only Matrix and Polygon registered one, so R’s default fired for the rest: it put a dim on the 2-element wrapper list (.xptr, .cpp) and kept the S3 class, so is.matrix(as.matrix(pitch)) was TRUE, no error was raised, the “matrix” held an external pointer instead of numbers, and printing it died inside the class’s own print(). One fallback method on the shared PraatObject class now returns the object’s own $as_matrix() where it has one (Sound, Pitch, Intensity, Spectrogram, Ltas, the tiers, the band-filtered spectrograms, … — bit-for-bit the numbers that accessor gives), and raises the package’s typed pladdrr_input_error naming the class and the accessor to use where it does not (Formant, PointProcess, TextGrid, Table, … have no matrix to give). as.matrix(Matrix) and as.matrix(Polygon) behave exactly as before.

  • matrix_read() and PitchTier$from_file() reject a file whose Object class = ... line names another class. A Praat text file names the C++ class to instantiate, and both readers cast the result to their own type without checking: loading a PitchTier as a Matrix reported garbage dimensions and then killed the R session uncatchably (SIGSEGV, exit 139) on the first value query, while a TextGrid cast to Matrix returned arbitrary heap values as numbers. They now raise the package’s tagged input error ([pladdrr_input_error:...], so with_pladdrr_errors() turns it into a catchable pladdrr_input_error) naming the file and the class found. Objects of a derived class still load (Sound or Ltas read as a Matrix), because the test is Praat’s own subclass rule (Thing_isa) and not a name match.

  • The same class check now guards the other door into a Matrix or PitchTier: the .xptr constructor argument. Matrix(.xptr = <a TextGrid pointer>) and PitchTier(.xptr = <a Matrix pointer>) used to build an object happily and die in the R process (SIGSEGV, exit 139, no tryCatch possible) on the first query, because the pointer was reinterpreted as the wrapper’s own C++ type before anything looked at it. Both now refuse a foreign object with the package’s typed pladdrr_input_error naming the class found, and because the check is Praat’s subclass test (Thing_isa), legitimate transfers — a Pitch converted to a PitchTier, an Ltas or Sound pointer taken as a Matrix — keep working. The other 37 .xptr-accepting constructors are still open (Sound, Pitch, Formant, Intensity, TextGrid, … segfault the same way); each needs its own one-line wiring, listed in audit/2026-11/fixes/F-xptr-door.md.

  • A WAV whose data chunk declares more bytes than the file holds (truncated download, malformed header) no longer allocates from that claim and pads the rest with zeros. Sound(path = ) now returns exactly the samples that are in the file, up to the end of the data chunk: a metadata chunk that follows the samples is no longer read back as audio either. It raises a pladdrr_data_loss condition naming the file and the real count, so options(pladdrr.data_loss = "error") turns a truncated file into an error and "silent" silences it. A 46-byte file whose header claimed 536 870 912 samples used to arrive as a 4.3 GB object; it now yields the one sample that is physically in it. The mirror case, a data chunk that understates the audio that follows it, still returns the shorter count Praat returns (design goal 1), but now reports the discarded samples through the same condition instead of only in Praat’s console text.

  • batch_process() no longer loses the whole run to one bad file. A file that cannot be read (a 0-byte .wav from an aborted download) or on which func fails produced a row with different columns from the measured rows, and the final rbind() then died with “names do not match previous names”: no results at all, and a message naming neither file nor cause. Every input file now yields exactly one row, in file order, a failure carrying its message in an error column and NA where the other rows have a measurement. That includes the pladdrr_data_loss error of a truncated WAV under options(pladdrr.data_loss = "error"), which used to abort the batch too.

  • An out-of-range channel is now an error instead of a wrong number. On a mono sound, Sound$get_mean(from, to, channel = 2) returned arbitrary heap contents (observed -6.8e+302) and larger indices could kill the R process; the same missing check in PointProcess$get_values_from_sound(), the LPC filter_inverse_at_time() entry points, LongSound$get_window_extrema() and LongSound$save_channel() silently produced another channel’s numbers, and Sound$to_point_process_extrema() / $to_point_process_zeros() counted extrema and zero crossings in whatever memory lay beyond the channel array (channel = 1000 killed the R session). An NA channel is named as such where the check happens in R (Sound$to_point_process_zeros(channel = NA) -> “channel must be a single integer, not NA”); where it happens in C++ the NA still arrives as its integer cast (Sound$get_mean(0, 1, NA) -> “Channel out of range [0, 3]: -2147483648”). None of these channel errors is classed: the R ones are plain simpleErrors and the C++ ones Rcpp::exception, so catch error, not pladdrr_input_error. channel = 0 keeps meaning “all channels” (Praat’s Vector_CHANNEL_AVERAGE) where Praat allows it; LongSound$get_window_extrema() is 1-based and LongSound$save_channel() keeps Praat’s 0 = left / 1 = right. Deviation from the application: Praat clamps an out-of-range channel to channel 1, pladdrr errors, because an error beats silent garbage.

  • Sound$get_maximum(from, to, channel) and Sound$get_minimum() now honour that documented channel argument; on a multichannel sound both used to return the extremum over all channels whatever channel was asked for. On a 3-channel file with per-channel peaks of 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, all three of get_maximum(0, 0, 1:3) returned 0.8999634 before and 0.09997559, 0.4999695, 0.8999634 now. The default became channel = 0 (all channels), so existing calls without a channel, and all single-channel results, are bit-identical. The channel argument is checked by the guards described in the previous bullet (an untagged error, not a pladdrr_input_error).

Performance and memory

  • The automatic thread count, and the default worker count of analyze_files_parallel() / process_sounds_parallel() / batch_process(), now follow the CPUs the process may use — the CPU affinity mask (taskset, container cpusets, SLURM) intersected with the cgroup CPU quota visible to the process — instead of the machine’s core count. The old default asked for the machine’s 32 threads no matter how few CPUs the process was given. Measured on a 32-core box (shared; medians of 3-5 runs over a 100-file pitch+formant corpus): in a 4-CPU cpuset analyze_files_parallel() with the default core count went from 4.57 s wall / 15.5 CPU-seconds to 1.81 s / 4.25 (-60 % wall, -73 % CPU-seconds — it was starting 31 CPU-bound workers on 4 CPUs), and a plain sequential loop from 2.08 s to 1.78 s with CPU-seconds unchanged. In a 16-CPU cpuset the saving is mostly latency, not CPU-seconds (loop 1.72 s -> 1.54 s, 4.39 -> 4.19 CPU-seconds; the batch helpers 1.72 s / 17.7 -> 1.18 s / 10.0), because with 16 usable CPUs the 32-thread default was mostly waiting rather than spinning. pladdrr_threads()$processors reports the same number, and explicit pladdrr_threads(n) / n_cores still win. Where the platform exposes no affinity or quota API (Windows, macOS) the count is unchanged; output is bit-identical either way.

  • The power-cepstrogram (CPPS) and Burg formant analyses no longer start a worker thread for a handful of frames. Sound$to_powercepstrogram() split a 3 s clip into 60-frame grains - 24 threads, 6x the CPU-seconds of the serial kernel and slower in wall clock than an 8-thread run; to_formant_burg() split it every 3 frames, so even a 0.25 s clip (40 frames) asked for 9 workers. The minimum work per thread is now 250 and 40 frames respectively (measured break-even times three and five; 10 of the 11 other LPC/formant sites already use 40, the eleventh uses 80), so short clips stay on one thread while long recordings still fill the machine. On 32 cores, one 3 s clip: 166 -> 27 CPU-ms (-83%) at 0.74x the wall time for the cepstrogram, 44 -> 30 CPU-ms (-32%) at 1.03x the wall time for formants; a 30 s recording is unchanged. Short clips pay for it in latency, which is the trade: over 600 clips at default settings, wall time per call went 1.26 -> 1.66 ms (+32%) for a 0.2 s formant analysis, 2.11 -> 3.22 ms (+53%) for a 0.4 s one and 1.85 -> 2.49 ms (+35%) for a 0.4 s cepstrogram, against CPU-seconds down 21-36% on the same calls; a 0.2 s cepstrogram and all pitch analysis are unaffected. If you analyse hundreds of sub-second clips and wall clock matters more than load, this change moves the wrong way for you. Output is bit-identical at every size, threads only partition frames.

pladdrr 5.0.6

Bug fixes

  • FormantPath$path_finder() now matches Praat. A SIMD branch clamped the frequency-change cost twice (capped at 0.01 instead of 1), so the Viterbi path, and the formants of extract_formant() after it, could differ from Praat by more than 1 kHz.

  • sound_extract_parts_pooled() no longer leaks segments: they are now ordinary R-owned Sounds (use_pool is accepted but ignored). A Sound from sound_pool_acquire() while the pool is full is now freed by R.

Performance and memory

  • Loading the package uses ~40 MB less resident memory per R process (including every parallel worker): Praat’s 42 MB object list is now constant-initialised instead of being written at load time.

  • Sound$resample() (and therefore every Burg formant analysis) runs its sinc interpolation on multiple threads; output is bit-identical.

  • process_sounds_parallel() on PSOCK clusters (Windows) no longer ships every Sound’s samples to every worker with each task.

  • as_data_frame() for Spectrogram, ComplexSpectrogram and Matrix fills preallocated vectors (peak memory roughly halved for long sounds).

  • sound_mean(), sound_min(), sound_max(), sound_rms() and sound_statistics() read channel 1 directly instead of exporting all channels.

  • Voice activity ZCR framing is O(frames + crossings) instead of O(frames x crossings).

  • AVQI frees the per-interval Sounds once they are concatenated.

Internal

  • Removed unused or unreachable SIMD code (pitch bridge, pitch filter, autocorrelation, window functions, SlopeSelector, cochleagram, excitation, FormantPath) and their internal test-only bindings.

  • Faithfulness registry: the Pitch (cc) and Pitch (AC) rows had been failing silently in the Praat oracle (a line wrap split the Praat command); fixed, and a FormantPath path-finder row was added.

pladdrr 5.0.5

Code quality

  • goodpractice style pass:
    • Wrapped all >80-character code lines in hand-written R/ files (auto-generated RcppExports.R unchanged); long string literals split into concatenated fragments with identical values.
    • Split five over-long functions into helpers (autolayer.TextGrid, analyze_files_parallel, plot.Matrix, plot.PowerCepstrum, two_pass_adaptive_pitch); the goodpractice function-length check now passes.
    • Consolidated cross-file @param blocks: dots docs kept in a single canonical file, constructor name docs inherited from a new pladdrr_shared_method_name anchor.
    • Removed the unused ._bust_cache PointProcess method; the 113 remaining complexity_unused_internal findings are documented false positives (S3 $ dispatch, S3 generics, roxygen anchors, Rcpp export surface) - see dev/goodpractice-dead-code-triage.md.
    • Test coverage raised 89.3% to 91.8%: added coverage-gap tests for input validation, empty-data warnings, dispatch fallback paths, and pladdrr.data_loss modes; not-testable guards (missing-ggplot2 stops, doc anchors, load-time branches) marked # nocov.
    • NEWS spelling fixes and inst/WORDLIST additions (dev, uncommented).

CRAN compliance

  • Removed the last two R CMD check warnings:
    • The compiled-code warning (stderr/stdout/_exit symbols in the vendored Praat objects): melder_console.cpp now routes console output through the R API (Rprintf/REprintf), gated to the main thread (R’s console API is unsafe off-main-thread, and Melder_casual can fire inside threaded DSP frame loops; worker-thread messages are dropped). All exit() call sites in Praat’s CLI paths throw a MelderError under PRAAT_LIB instead of terminating the process.
    • The non-portable PKG_CXXFLAGS flag -ffp-contract=off was replaced by a source-level #pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF in the vendored melder.h (included by every DSP translation unit) — the same bit-exactness guarantee with no compiler flags.
  • Removed the R-devel “package has both src/Makevars.in and src/Makevars” NOTE: the cleanup script now deletes the configure-generated src/Makevars from the build copy.
  • Expanded inst/WORDLIST and fixed a typo; the documentation now passes spelling::spell_check_package().
  • Modernized the test suite (~440 assertion conversions: expect_gt/gte/ lt/lte, expect_length, expect_named, expect_type, expect_s3_class, expect_identical for exact integer comparisons, expect_false, fixed = TRUE on literal patterns, anyNA).
  • Parallel batch functions (analyze_files_parallel(), process_sounds_parallel()) now cap their automatic core count at 2 under R CMD check (honoring _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_), so the default-n_cores tests pass CRAN’s process-spawn limit while dev/CI still uses all cores.
  • Fixed a broken example in the textgrid_create() docs (an uncommented continuation line) that made R CMD check fail to run any examples.
  • Documented the ... argument on plot.*, as.data.frame.*, print.*, and summary.* methods, and synced the shared pladdrr_shared_* parameter docs with their usage — clears the “Rd sections” warning.

pladdrr 5.0.4

Bug fixes

  • The Praat interpreter entry points (praat_run_script(),

  • The Praat interpreter entry points (praat_run_script(), praat_eval_numeric(), praat_eval_string(), praat_eval_vector(), praat_eval_matrix(), praat_eval_string_array(), and PraatInterpreter$run()/$eval()/$set_variable()) now reject NULL, empty, non-scalar, or non-character inputs with a clear R error instead of an opaque C++ failure.

  • Sound$to_textgrid_silences() accepted min_silent_duration / min_sounding_duration but silently ignored them (a TODO). It now merges short silent and sounding intervals via the same IntervalTier_cutIntervals_minimumDuration + IntervalTier_combineIntervalsOnLabelMatch passes the intensity-based path already used.

  • PointProcess(tmin, tmax) now creates an empty PointProcess (previously it only accepted an internal pointer and stopped otherwise). Backed by a new pointprocess_module$create_empty() C++ factory wrapping Praat’s PointProcess_create(). Enables empty-object batch operations.

  • praat_eval_string_array("empty$# (n)") segfaulted the R session. The vendored Praat do_empty_STRVEC built its result with autoSTRVEC result { n }, which zero-initialises the vector and so leaves every element a null pointer instead of a valid empty C string; the R wrapper’s Melder_peek32to8() then dereferenced null. It now returns n empty strings. Also un-skipped formant$save() (its earlier segfault was a symptom of the fixed to_formant_burg() crash).

  • Sound$get_optimal_formant_ceiling() and Sound$to_formant_optimal() crashed the R session (SIGTRAP / “irrecoverable exception”) for every input. Two stacked causes were fixed. (1) The vendored Praat Sound_to_Formant_common read the null output sound instead of the local resampled when setting up the short-term analysis and Formant/LPC objects, crashing every Burg/robust formant-analysis entry point (to_formant_burg() was also broken). (2) The pladdrr Formant_extractPart stub wrote newFrame->formant[] without allocating it — Formant_create zeroes frames so the array is null — so the interval path aborted on the first dereference. to_formant_burg(), to_formant_optimal(), and get_optimal_formant_ceiling() now all work.

  • autoplot.Spectrogram(), autolayer.Spectrogram(), and plot.Spectrogram() scrambled the frequency axis for any non-square spectrogram matrix (a expand.grid()/as.vector() row/column-major mismatch — a 220 Hz tone rendered with its peak at 2201 Hz), and plotted raw linear power directly as if already in dB, making the dynamic_range clipping parameter a silent no-op.

  • plot_powercepstrogram() had the same two defects (time/quefrency-axis transposition and missing power-to-dB conversion), plus a hardcoded max_time <- 5.0 placeholder in place of the cepstrogram’s real duration.

  • plot_cpp_timeseries() used the same hardcoded-duration placeholder, and a tryCatch() scoping bug (cpp_values[i] <- NA instead of <<- inside the error handler) meant a failed per-time-point CPP query silently became 0 instead of being dropped as NA.

  • plot_powercepstrum() used a hardcoded max_quefrency <- 0.05 placeholder instead of the cepstrum’s real quefrency range, and plotted its power_dB column (misleadingly named — the values are raw linear power, not dB) without converting, putting the line trace and its own peak-prominence marker on incompatible scales.

    None of these 5 functions had any test coverage before this release; 12 new regression tests were added (test-spectrogram-plot-regression.R, test-cepstrum-plots-regression.R).

  • Follow-up fixes closing the remaining power_dB-mislabel call sites: autoplot.PowerCepstrum()/autolayer.PowerCepstrum() and plot.PowerCepstrum() still plotted the C++ as_data_frame()’s misleadingly-named power_dB column (raw linear power) directly under a “Power (dB)” axis, and selected their cepstral-peak marker with which.max() on linear power. Both now convert to a real dB power_db column before plotting (5 new tests in test-powercepstrum-db-regression.R).

  • plot_powercepstrogram(show_cpp_contour = TRUE) drew its CPP-contour overlay as a flat line at a hardcoded quefrency = 0.01 placeholder; it now overlays the real per-time-frame cepstral-peak quefrency, computed as the argmax of each frame’s own raster row.

  • plot.Spectrogram()’s preemphasis argument (default 50) was accepted but never referenced; removed as dead — pre-emphasis belongs in the DSP layer, not a plot method.

  • plot_cpp_timeseries() no longer emits a cosmetic “Mean CPP: NaN dB (SD: NA)” subtitle when every sample fails; it now shows “No samples”.

  • PowerCepstrum$as_data_frame() (the C++ RPowerCepstrum module) returned a column misleadingly named power_dB that actually held raw linear power; renamed to the honest power. This is a breaking change for any caller that read $as_data_frame()$power_dB directly; the affected plotting functions now read power and convert to power_db.

  • as.data.frame.LPC() indexed the coefficient matrix as if it were a flat list (coeffs[[i]]), so it emitted one row per frame with a single mislabeled coefficient and silently dropped the other maxnCoefficients - 1 coefficients of every frame. It now reads each frame’s coefficient column (coeffs[, i]), yielding one row per (frame, coefficient) as documented.

  • AmplitudeTier$to_intensity_tier() and AmplitudeTier$save() called non-existent internal wrappers (.amplitudetier_to_intensitytier() / .amplitudetier_save()), so both errored with “could not find function”. They now dispatch through the Rcpp module (to_intensity_tier_ptr() / save()). Six get_shimmer_*() AmplitudeTier methods were also removed: shimmer is a PointProcess metric (already present there), and these AmplitudeTier copies had no C++ implementation.

  • plot_spectrogram_pitch()’s freq_max argument (documented “Maximum frequency to display”) was silently ignored — it was passed to plot.Spectrogram(), which has no such parameter. It now maps to plot.Spectrogram()’s to_freq, so the frequency cap is honored.

  • plot_sound_pitch()’s pitch_floor/pitch_ceiling arguments were dead — passed to plot.Pitch(), which ignores them. Removed.

  • Deprecated get_intensity_at_time()’s interpolate argument and create_sound()’s start_time argument were silently ignored; both now forward to the underlying R6 methods.

  • plot.Pitch()/autoplot.Pitch()’s show_voicing argument never colored by voicing strength: it looked for a voicing_strength column, but Pitch$as_data_frame() names it strength (and only includes it with include_strength = TRUE). Both now pull the strength column and color by it.

  • autolayer.PointProcess()’s ymin/ymax arguments were ignored (it used geom_vline), autoplot.PCA()/autoplot.Discriminant()’s garnish argument was dead, and .formant_colors()’s max_formant was redundant. All now honor their documented behavior.

pladdrr 5.0.1

New features

  • Added autoplot() and autolayer() S3 methods for 27 previously unsupported Praat object classes: AmplitudeTier, DurationTier, IntensityTier, PitchTier, FormantTier, FormantGrid, FormantPath, Excitation, ComplexSpectrogram, Cepstrum, Cochleagram, PowerCepstrogram, MFCC, LFCC, BarkSpectrogram, MelSpectrogram, Matrix, PCA, Discriminant, FormantModeler, Electroglottogram, LongSound, DTW, Polygon, VocalTract, LPC, KlattGrid.
  • Added as.data.frame() S3 methods for 15 classes that lacked them.

Bug fixes

  • process_sounds_parallel() shipped already-loaded Sound objects directly to Windows PSOCK workers; their external pointer to the underlying C++ object cannot survive that process boundary, causing spurious errors on Windows with n_cores > 1. Sounds are now serialized to raw sample data and reconstructed inside each worker.
  • Fixed FormantGrid$as_data_frame() missing required time_step argument.
  • autoplot.KlattGrid()/as.data.frame.KlattGrid() passed a formant-type name as a string where the underlying accessor required an integer code, producing empty plots or silently wrong data for every formant type. Fixed to map the name to its integer code before dispatch; also corrected the shared formant_type documentation, which claimed "all" was an accepted value for autolayer.KlattGrid() when only autoplot.KlattGrid() actually supports it.
  • as.data.frame.Cochleagram() always errored.
  • as.data.frame.LPC() always errored, due to a typo’d power_dB column name that did not exist on the object.
  • autolayer.DTW() plotted the wrong columns and crashed on some NULL-valued paths.
  • autoplot/autolayer/as.data.frame for Matrix, BarkSpectrogram, and MelSpectrogram plotted raw row/column bin indices instead of the real time/frequency axis values.
  • autoplot.Cepstrum() defaulted to a power-cepstrum dB view; Praat’s actual default is a raw signed quefrency-domain view. Fixed the default and added a power parameter to select the dB view explicitly.
  • autoplot.ComplexSpectrogram() and autolayer.ComplexSpectrogram() both mislabeled linear amplitude values as dB and ignored dynamic_range.
  • as.data.frame.VocalTract(), autoplot.VocalTract(), and autolayer.VocalTract() all hardcoded section spacing (dx) instead of reading it from the object, giving wrong x-axis values whenever spacing was non-default.
  • autoplot.FormantTier()/autolayer.FormantTier() defaulted to an interpolated line view; Praat’s actual default view is speckle (points).
  • autoplot.FormantPath() and autoplot.FormantModeler() always produced empty plots — the former from a column-name mismatch, the latter from a wide/long data-frame format mismatch.
  • as.data.frame.PowerCepstrogram() called a nonexistent $as_data_frame() method and always crashed; fixed to route through $to_matrix().
  • Sound$extract_electroglottogram() was never registered in the R6 method table, despite its underlying C++ export existing and being registered; every call crashed with “attempt to apply non-function”.

pladdrr 5.0.0

Bug fixes

  • intensity_tier_to_amplitude_tier() and amplitude_tier_from_point_process() read $.pointer off IntensityTier/PointProcess/Sound objects, but those classes store their external pointer under $.xptr ($.pointer is only an alias on AmplitudeTier). The mismatch resolved to NULL and failed deep in the C++ layer with R_ExternalPtrAddr: argument of type NILSXP is not an external pointer. Fixed both call sites to use $.xptr.
  • matrix_read() called an internal .matrix_read() binding that did not exist, so every call failed with could not find function ".matrix_read" (silently masked by an R CMD check NOTE-suppression entry in utils::globalVariables(), not by a real implementation). Added the missing C++ binding (mirroring the existing PitchTier/IntensityTier/ TextGrid read pattern) and wired up Matrix$save() to the C++ save method that already existed but was never exposed to R.
  • get_max_pitch()/get_min_pitch() (deprecated legacy wrappers) called Pitch$get_maximum()/get_minimum() with a stale interpolation = argument; the current method signature takes interpolate = (logical). Every call failed with unused argument (interpolation = "none"). Fixed to pass interpolate = FALSE.
  • get_formant_at_time()/get_mean_formant()’s documentation pointed users to extract_formants() as the source of a compatible object, but extract_formants() no longer produces one when given an R6 Sound object (it delegates to sound$to_formant_burg(), returning an R6 Formant object instead) — a stale cross-reference left over from the package’s S3-to-R6 migration. No behavior changed; documentation now describes the actual expected input and extract_formants()’s actual return value on both its code paths.

Documentation

  • Removed performance claims (absolute and relative) from DESCRIPTION and README.md per CRAN submission review, including comparisons to other tools such as Parselmouth. Historical changelog entries with benchmark data have been moved to NEWS-archive.md, which is not shipped in the package tarball.
  • Reconciled the Praat module count reported in DESCRIPTION (37 to 38) to match the actual number of exposed Rcpp modules.

Memory

  • Reworked spectral moments batch calculations to compute centre of gravity, standard deviation, skewness, and kurtosis directly from the spectrogram data, removing intermediate per-frame allocations. Results are numerically identical to previous versions.
  • Pre-allocated the output vectors used to build formant and pitch data frames, and made pitch data frame construction skip allocating the strength/intensity columns when they are not requested.
